newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China-backed paper in Hong Kong blasts Patten.
newsitem.headline: China-backed paper in Hong Kong blasts Patten.

text.p: A China-backed newspaper launched a stinging attack on governor Chris Patten on Saturday over his remark about some Hong Kong people lobbying Beijing to interfere in the territory's policy matters.
Patten had said in his final policy address on Wednesday that people in the colony who appealed to Beijing on various issues were inviting China's interference in Hong Kong policy matters.
He said this would undermine its autonomy after Britain hands back the territory at midnight on June 30, 1997.
The China-backed newspaper Wen Wei Po said Patten's behavour was "despicable" in accusing some people who tried to protect the interests of Hong Kong by expressing their views to Beijing.

The newspaper said Patten should be able to distinguish between expressing views on Hong Kong and "making surreptitous appeals," which it said implied the kind of money politics and corruption found in British politics.
British newspapers recently reported that Members of Parliament had accepted payments to ask questions on behalf of various companies, it said.
From the 1950s to the 1980s, British companies often lobbied in London to ensure their special status in the colony, the Hong Kong newspaper said.
"This colonialist applies what he considers as a normal practice to imply that Hong Kong people will do the same when they are reflecting their views to Beijing. It is unfair," Wen Wei Po said.
